lines.say: An emerging disease is new, or rapidly increasing in cases or range.
COVID-19 is an example. So is Ebola appearing in new regions.
A re-emerging disease was under control, but it's coming back.
Outbreak, then epidemic, then pandemic, as it spreads further.

items.text: endemic: always present at a steady level

lines.say: RNA viruses like influenza mutate quickly. Their copying enzymes don't fix errors.
Antigenic drift is small changes building up in surface antigens.

draw.alt: Virus antigens slowly change shape so antibodies fit less well

lines.say: Old antibodies fit less well. That's why flu vaccines are updated.
Antigenic shift is sudden. Two strains swap whole gene segments in one cell.
Antibiotics select for bacteria that already carry resistance.
A zoonosis passes from animals to humans. The jump is called spillover.
Hendra virus lives in flying foxes. That's the reservoir.

draw.alt: Hendra virus: flying fox to horse to human

lines.say: Horses catch it, and people have caught it from close contact with horses.
Zoonoses are hard to wipe out. The pathogen survives in the animals.
A vector carries a pathogen between hosts. Mosquitoes spread Ross River virus.
A traveller can cross the world in a day, before symptoms even show.

draw.alt: One case spreads to many cities by flights

lines.say: Trade moves animals, food and even mosquito eggs in containers.
But globalisation also helps. Scientists share genome data fast.

frames.heading: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander knowledge

lines.say: First Nations peoples hold deep knowledge of plants for health and healing.
Plants have been used for wounds, pain, coughs and as antiseptics.
Some contain antimicrobial compounds that could become new medicines.
Research needs free, prior and informed consent, recognition, and shared benefits.
Surveillance. Doctors report notifiable diseases, so a rise gets noticed.
Identify the pathogen with PCR and genome sequencing.
Contact tracing finds who an infected person met.

draw.alt: Contact tracing: a case and its contacts, isolated and quarantined

lines.say: Isolate the sick. Quarantine contacts who may be in the incubation period.
Vaccinate, improve hygiene, control vectors, and vaccinate animals like horses.
Emerging includes old diseases spreading to new places.
Antibiotics don't cause mutations. They select resistant bacteria.
Drift is gradual. Shift is sudden.
First Nations knowledge is living knowledge, not just history.
